text:
martin: Heads-up: onboarding sampleapp failing with 403 when calling embeddings.create from the Node SDK but curl works. Looks like an OAuth scope mismatch.

kai: can you paste the exact calls?

martin: repro: REST (works):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/embeddings.create -d '{"input":"hi"}'
# -> 200
```
SDK (403):
```
await client.embeddings.create({ input: 'hi' })
# -> 403 "insufficient_scope"
```
Token looks identical. I dug into logs and server rejects scope 'embeddings.write' but accepts 'embeddings.generate'. Our auth docs say "embeddings" scope, but server auth layer recently split write/generate scopes.

anya: ugh. that explains a few support tickets. Two things: (1) docs and token issuance flow need updating, (2) SDK should surface a clearer error hint when auth scope is rejected (e.g., suggest which scope is required). Right now the 403 is opaque.

kai: Agreed. Also noticed a second parity nit: SDK accepts "temp" as the param name in older apps, but server expects "temperature" now. If you pass temp in SDK it maps to temperature, but the Node SDK's types were updated and now reject unknown params instead of mapping aliases. That broke a sampleapp that set temp=0.7 and now gets a validation error.

martin: yes, sampleapp uses temp in the quickstart config. When the SDK started rejecting unknown keys it surfaced the server change too early. New users copy the quickstart and crash.

anya: plan: (A) add an alias map in SDK for common legacy param names (temp -> temperature, topP -> top_p), but emit a deprecation warning when alias is used. (B) update onboarding docs to prefer canonical names and add a migration note.

kai: also found a third subtle drift: server changed the default model variant for "redwood-chat" from "v1" to "v1-rl" and REST returns a server-chosen variant header x-model-variant when omitted; SDK used to surface that header in response metadata, but we removed response metadata in a patch. Sampleapp relied on that header to decide which eval set to run. So sampleapp now runs the wrong eval and flags a regression.

martin: wow. multiple places failing: auth, param aliasing, missing response metadata. Can we be defensive in SDK? Surface response headers in a metadata object, and add a clear auth-scope error with a hint like: "required scopes: embeddings.generate".

anya: yes. Also add a temporary compatibility flag allow_legacy_aliases=true for minor releases so we don't break users immediately. We'll log telemetry on alias usage and scope-mismatch errors so we can measure prevalence.

kai: I'll open DX-520 with the plan: 1) update token docs and token issuer to include new scopes or map old tokens to include both, 2) add alias mapping + deprecation warnings, 3) re-add response metadata with x-model-variant, 4) improve 403 error hints.

martin: thanks. can we also add a quickstart CI job that uses an older sampleapp config (temp param + no explicit model variant) to catch these regressions?

anya: good idea. I'll add a test matrix entry for legacy-configs.

sdk-bot: jira:DX-520 created by kai - "SDK parity: oauth scope hints + legacy param aliases + response metadata + quickstart legacy CI" :white_check_mark:

martin: thanks team. will re-run onboarding once patches land and report back. :rocket:
